---
title: "Payments Retry Service — traceable engineering"
---

This small project shows the canonical Quarto-Needs workflow on an ordinary
engineering problem: a payment retry service. One stakeholder need drives a
small requirement set; one architecture decision bounds the solution; tests
and evidence verify the requirements. Everything below is declared in this
repository and every table, matrix, flow, and graph on this page is generated
from those declarations at build time.

## The stakeholder need

::: {.need #STK-001 type="stakeholder-need" status="approved"}
## Reliable payments under transient failures

Customers must not lose a paid order because a payment provider hiccupped.

### Rationale

Failed retries generate support tickets, refunds, and churn; the business
wants providers to absorb transient faults instead.
:::

## Requirements

::: {.need #REQ-001 type="system-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" derives-from="STK-001" implemented-by="COMP-001" verified-by="TC-001"}
## Retry transient provider failures

The service shall retry a payment up to three times when the provider
returns a transient error.

### Rationale

Transient faults are the most common failure mode and are safely retryable.
:::

::: {.need #REQ-002 type="system-requirement" status="approved" priority="high" derives-from="STK-001" implemented-by="COMP-001" verified-by="TC-002"}
## Never double-charge a retried payment

The service shall use an idempotency key so a retried payment cannot be
charged twice.

### Rationale

A retry that double-charges is worse than the fault it recovers from.
:::

::: {.need #REQ-003 type="system-requirement" status="approved" priority="medium" derives-from="STK-001" implemented-by="COMP-002" verified-by="TC-003"}
## Expose retry outcomes to operations

The service shall record every attempt's outcome so operations can inspect
retry behaviour.

### Rationale

Operations cannot trust what it cannot observe.
:::

::: {.need #REQ-004 type="system-requirement" status="approved" priority="low" derives-from="STK-001" implemented-by="COMP-002" verified-by="TC-004"}
## Bound the retry backlog

The service shall cap the pending-retry queue so sustained outages cannot
exhaust storage.

### Rationale

A backlog without bounds turns a provider outage into a platform incident.
:::

## Architecture

::: {.need #ADR-001 type="architecture-decision" status="accepted" addresses="REQ-001; REQ-002" applies-to="COMP-001; COMP-002"}
## Retry through an idempotent client with a bounded queue

Retries live in a dedicated client holding the idempotency key; a bounded
queue decouples request handling from provider latency.

### Rationale

Centralizing retries in one component keeps the double-charge guarantee in
one place instead of scattering it across call sites.
:::

::: {.need #COMP-001 type="component" status="approved"}
## Retry client

Owns provider calls, the idempotency key, and the retry schedule.
:::

::: {.need #COMP-002 type="component" status="approved"}
## Retry ledger

Persists attempt outcomes and enforces the pending-retry bound.
:::

## Verification

::: {.need #TC-001 type="test-case" status="passed" evidences="EVD-001"}
## Transient failures are retried

Simulates two transient provider errors followed by success.
:::

::: {.need #TC-002 type="test-case" status="passed" evidences="EVD-002"}
## Retries never double-charge

Replays the same idempotency key and asserts a single charge.
:::

::: {.need #TC-003 type="test-case" status="passed" evidences="EVD-003"}
## Outcomes are recorded

Forces each outcome class and checks the ledger entries.
:::

::: {.need #TC-004 type="test-case" status="passed" evidences="EVD-001"}
## Backlog bound holds

Floods the queue past its cap and asserts rejection instead of growth.
:::
